newsitem.title: USA: Israel, Lebanon list cease-fire violations.
newsitem.headline: Israel, Lebanon list cease-fire violations.

text.p: Israel and Lebanon accused each other of violating a five-month ceasefire during a three-day monitoring committee meeting in the Lebanese coastal town of Naquora this week, the U.S. State Department said on Wednesday.

Three Lebanese complaints involved Israeli shelling of civilian areas and the expulsion of citizens, while Israel complained that Hizbollah forces used civilian-populated areas as mortar launching sites, the department said in a written statement.

"The monitoring group called on all parties to desist in all circumstances from any shelling which is disproportionate and indiscriminate, or directly or indirectly puts in danger the lives of civilians and the safety of populated villages," it said.
The five-nation group -- France, Syria, Lebanon, Israel and the United States -- also urged all parties "to adopt restraint and caution in military operations" in the vicinity of populated areas.
In addition, the statement said the issue of civilian expulsions would be addressed no later than Oct. 15.
The committee was set up to deal with violations of a U.S.-brokered ceasefire that ended a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon in April.

The ceasefire understanding banned firing from or at civilian targets on both sides of the Israeli-Lebanon border, but did not prohibit guerrilla attacks on Israeli forces occupying southern Lebanon and gave both sides the right to self-defence.
